summary: The core priority right now is executing the seven-month SEO/AI-search visibility push behind Asia Star and Intelligent China, while the Knowledge website redesign settles into a final round of feedback and a lingering Outlook lockout needs clearing before it disrupts the team.
summaryDetail: The biggest initiative in motion is the global marketing strategy set on June 30: a seven-month SEO and AI-search visibility program that puts Asia Star and Intelligent China first, with US partner programs (Berkeley as a possible third) pushed into a secondary audit phase and Stanford/Columbia on hold for the quarter. That work now hinges on Joseph — he owes the target areas/prompts and audience focus document, the Asia Star participant and CRM hot-lead analysis, and a brief on Google Ads conversion tracking — and the team still needs to launch the Intelligent China webpage and drive traffic to it, so these are the items to watch this week. On the Knowledge website redesign, the team has landed on a direction (keep the two-menu structure, pinned-article-plus-latest layout, BCI/BSI index banners in the Knowledge section, videos dispersed by topic, no stock ticker) and needs a 30-minute working session to mark final feedback, with Joseph sharing his HTML and Joker revising accordingly. Urgent housekeeping: the Outlook account lockout from stale password caches still needs resolution — everyone must delete and re-login on all devices, update the home computer, and confirm the backend unlock with JSB. Looking ahead, the team is lining up external visibility — the European Chamber Silver Economy event on Oct 29, the SwissCham Sino-Swiss Economic Forum cooperation email, and Andrea and Katya's spotlight videos for LinkedIn and YouTube.
